details.readme:
# T3 Code

T3 Code is an "agent harness control surface". It enables control of the agents on your machine with a best-in-class mobile app ([iOS](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/t3-code-remote-claude-more/id6787819824), [Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.t3tools.t3code)), [web app](https://app.t3.codes) and [Electron-based desktop app](https://t3.codes).

Works with your subscriptions on Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok Build, OpenCode, Google Antigravity, and fx. If they're set up on your computer, T3 Code can control them.

## "Wait, what are you selling me?"

Nothing. We built T3 Code because we wanted the best possible development experience with agents. We were inspired by existing solutions like the Codex desktop app, Conductor, Claude Desktop and Cursor Glass, but none met our bar.

We wanted something performant, remote-ready, and truly open. If we ever go the wrong direction, we want you to have everything you need to fork and build the editor that you want.

## Installation

> [!WARNING]
> T3 Code currently supports Codex, Claude, Cursor, Grok Build, OpenCode, Antigravity, and fx. Install and authenticate at least one provider before use:
>
> - Codex: install [Codex CLI](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli) and run `codex login`
> - Claude: install [Claude Code](https://claude.com/product/claude-code) and run `claude auth login`
> - Cursor: install [Cursor CLI](https://cursor.com/cli) and run `agent login`
> - Grok Build: install [Grok Build CLI](https://x.ai/cli) and run `grok login`
> - OpenCode: install [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) and run `opencode auth login`
> - Antigravity: enable it in Settings, then use **Install Antigravity** and **Sign in with Google**. No CLI is required.
> - fx: install [fx](https://fx.sh) and run `fx login` on the machine running the T3 Code server ([setup guide](./docs/user/providers-fx.md))

### Command line

```bash
curl -fsSL https://t3.codes/install.sh | sh
```

On Windows, in PowerShell:

```powershell
irm https://t3.codes/install.ps1 | iex
```

Then run `t3` to start the server and open the local web app. `t3 service install` keeps it running in the background, `t3 update` moves to a newer release, and `t3 --help` has the full reference.

To try it once without installing, run `npx t3@latest` instead.

### Desktop app

Install the latest version of the desktop app from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/releases), or from your favorite package registry:

#### Windows (`winget`)

```bash
winget install T3Tools.T3Code
```

#### Windows (`scoop`)

```bash
scoop install extras/t3code
```

#### macOS (Homebrew)

```bash
brew install --cask t3-code
```

#### Debian, Ubuntu (`.deb`)

Download the `.deb` from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/releases), then:

```bash
sudo apt install ./T3-Code-*.deb
```

#### Arch Linux (AUR)

Stable:

```bash
yay -S t3code-bin
```

Nightly:

```bash
yay -S t3code-nightly-bin
```

The AUR packaging is maintained in this repository under [`packaging/aur`](./packaging/aur).

#### Nix (nixpkgs)

```bash
nix profile add github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable#t3code
```

The package is maintained in [nixpkgs](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/tree/nixos-unstable/pkgs/by-name/t3/t3code)
and includes the desktop app (`t3code-desktop`) and the `t3` command.
See [Nix installation](./docs/user/install.md#nix-nixpkgs) for NixOS configuration and updates.

## Some notes

We are very very early in this project. Expect bugs.

We are (mostly) not accepting contributions yet. Small fixes may be considered. Big features will not be.

## Documentation

Full docs live in [docs/](./docs). There's no docs site yet.

- [FAQ](./docs/user/faq.md)
- [Install and first run](./docs/user/install.md)
- [Permission modes](./docs/user/permission-modes.md)
- [Keyboard shortcuts](./docs/user/keybindings.md)
- [Project settings](./docs/user/project-settings.md)
- [Appearance preferences](./docs/user/appearance.md)
- [Remote access from a phone or another machine](./docs/user/remote-access.md)
- [Connect Claude Code, Codex, ChatGPT and other agents over MCP](./docs/user/outside-agents.md)
- [Keeping app and server in sync](./docs/user/updating.md)
- [Source control integrations](./docs/user/source-control.md)
- Multiple accounts: [Codex](./docs/user/providers-codex.md) · [Claude](./docs/user/providers-claude.md)
- [Run T3 Code as a background service](./docs/user/background-service.md)

Building from source? Start at [docs/internals/overview.md](./docs/internals/overview.md).

## If you REALLY want to contribute still.... read this first

### Install `vp`

T3 Code uses Vite+ so you'll need to install the global `vp` command-line tool.

#### macOS / Linux

```bash
curl -fsSL https://vite.plus | bash
```

#### Windows

```bash
irm https://vite.plus/ps1 | iex
```

Checkout their getting started guide for more information: https://viteplus.dev/guide/

### Install dependencies

```bash
vp i
```

Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) before reporting a bug or opening a PR.

Have a feature request? Start an [Ideas discussion](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/discussions/categories/ideas).

Need support? Join the [Discord](https://discord.gg/jn4EGJjrvv).

details.readme:
# agent-desktop Computer use for AI agents: read and operate desktop apps through the OS accessibility tree.

A CLI and C library for macOS, Windows and Linux. A snapshot returns JSON with a ref for every element an agent can act on. The agent acts on a ref and snapshots again to check, with no pixel matching; the loop stays in your agent. Every CLI call runs in its own process. Headless calls still prohibit foreground activation and synthesized input. Snapshots, clipboard reads, screenshots, command output and debug artifacts can contain private desktop content. Keep them out of public logs and uploads. The optional [JEV helper](skills/jev-desktop/SKILL.md) sends screen descriptions to a configured model provider; it is separate from the native CLI. See [privacy and data handling](docs/faq.md#what-data-can-contain-private-information). ## Installation Install on macOS, Windows or Linux with npm: ```bash npm install -g agent-desktop agent-desktop version ``` Bun, Yarn and pnpm can install the same package. It includes native binaries and platform helpers for x64 and ARM64. For direct execution without a JavaScript launcher, download the matching native archive from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-desktop/releases) and keep its helper beside the executable. Official Homebrew and Scoop packages are being submitted; they are not yet available in the default catalogs. The repository no longer maintains a custom Homebrew tap or Scoop bucket. - **macOS** needs Accessibility permission: `agent-desktop permissions --guide`. - **Windows** needs no grant for apps at your terminal's integrity level. - **Linux** needs the user's graphical session with `at-spi2-core`. See [installation and permissions](docs/install.md) for package-manager behavior, release archives, and building from source. ## Quick start Observe, act on a ref, observe again. Any app name from `agent-desktop list-apps` works; Finder is the macOS example. Each command prints one JSON envelope; a trimmed snapshot follows the commands. ```bash agent-desktop snapshot --app Finder -i # interactive elements, each with a ref agent-desktop click @s8f3k2p9:e8 # act on a ref from that snapshot agent-desktop snapshot --app Finder -i # observe again to verify ``` ```json { "version": "2.6", "ok": true, "command": "snapshot", "data": { "app": "Finder", "window": { "id": "w-204749", "title": "Downloads" }, "snapshot_id": "s8f3k2p9", "ref_count": 59, "complete": true, "tree": { "role": "window", "name": "Downloads", "children": [ { "role": "treeitem", "name": "Documents", "ref_id": "@s8f3k2p9:e8", "available_actions": ["Click"] } ] } } } ``` - **Refs belong to their snapshot.** A bare `@e8` is rejected with `INVALID_ARGS`. When the UI changes, an action returns `STALE_REF` or `AMBIGUOUS_TARGET`: take a new snapshot and use its refs. - **Several windows** give `AMBIGUOUS_TARGET`; `snapshot` lists the candidate window ids in `error.details`. Pass one with `--window-id`. - **Dense apps:** map first with `snapshot --skeleton --app Slack -i --compact`, then drill into one region with `snapshot --root @s8f3k2p9:e3 -i --compact`. - **Headless by default.** Ref actions go through the accessibility API without moving the pointer or taking focus. The global `--headed` flag allows physical input. - **PowerShell.** Quote every ref (`'@s8f3k2p9:e8'`), because a bare `@token` is the splatting operator. ## For AI agents The binary carries its own docs, matched to its version: ```bash agent-desktop skills get desktop # the loop, refs, verification and retry rules agent-desktop skills get platform # what differs on the OS you run on agent-desktop --help # flags for one command ``` Install the skill into an agent harness from [skills.sh](https://skills.sh/vercel-labs/agent-desktop/agent-desktop): ```bash npx skills add https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-desktop --skill agent-desktop ``` Or add this to your `AGENTS.md`: ```markdown Use `agent-desktop` to see and operate desktop apps. Before the first use, run `agent-desktop skills get desktop` and `agent-desktop skills get platform`, and follow them. ``` Every command prints one envelope with `ok` and either `data` or `error`. An error carries a `code`, a `disposition` and usually a `suggestion`; retry only when `error.disposition.retry` is `safe`. The contract, error codes and exit codes are in [docs/json-output.md](docs/json-output.md). ## Commands It ships 60 command names, 56 operational commands. The other four (`key-down`, `key-up`, `mouse-down`, `mouse-up`) refuse to run until a daemon can release a held key or button. | Group | Commands | |---|---| | Observe | `snapshot`, `find`, `get`, `is`, `screenshot`, `list-surfaces` | | Act on a ref | `click`, `double-click`, `triple-click`, `right-click`, `type`, `set-value`, `clear`, `focus`, `select`, `toggle`, `check`, `uncheck`, `expand`, `collapse`, `scroll`, `scroll-to` | | Keyboard and mouse | `press`, `hover`, `drag`, `mouse-move`, `mouse-click`, `mouse-wheel`, `key-down`, `key-up`, `mouse-down`, `mouse-up` | | Apps and windows | `launch`, `close-app`, `list-apps`, `list-windows`, `list-displays`, `focus-window`, `resize-window`, `move-window`, `minimize`, `maximize`, `restore`, `open-system-surface` | | Notifications | `list-notifications`, `dismiss-notification`, `dismiss-all-notifications`, `notification-action` | | Clipboard | `clipboard-get`, `clipboard-set`, `clipboard-clear` | | Wait | `wait` | | Sessions | `session`, `trace`, `cursor-overlay` | | System | `status`, `permissions`, `version`, `batch`, `skills` | ## Platform support | | macOS | Windows | Linux | |---|:---:|:---:|:---:| | Accessibility tree | Yes | Yes | Yes (AT-SPI) | | Click / type / keyboard | Yes | Yes | AT-SPI; X11 / GNOME keys | | Mouse input | Yes | Yes | X11, `--headed` | | Screenshot | Yes | Yes | X11 windows; Wayland portal | | Clipboard | Yes | Yes | Yes; Wayland needs `wl-clipboard` | | App & window management | Yes | Yes | Launch/list; X11 window control | | Notifications | Yes | Yes | GNOME Shell | | Shell surfaces (`open-system-surface`) | Dock, menu bar extras | Yes | GNOME tray, Action Center | The Windows surface and `launch` notes and the Linux X11 and Wayland notes are in [docs/install.md](docs/install.md#platform-notes). `agent-desktop skills get platform` prints the full capability table for the OS you run on. ## Language bindings Each release also ships `libagent_desktop_ffi` for macOS, Linux and Windows, so a program can call the tool in process instead of starting the CLI for each command. `agent-desktop skills get ffi` covers the entry points, memory ownership and threading rules. ```python import ctypes lib = ctypes.CDLL("./lib/libagent_desktop_ffi.dylib") lib.ad_adapter_create.restype = ctypes.c_void_p lib.ad_adapter_destroy.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p] assert lib.ad_init(7) == 0 # AD_RESULT_OK when the header's AD_ABI_VERSION_MAJOR matches the library adapter = lib.ad_adapter_create() lib.ad_adapter_destroy(adapter) ``` ## Development Each platform adapter builds only on its own OS, so scope cargo to the host's packages. On macOS: ```bash HOST_PKGS=(-p agent-desktop-core -p agent-desktop-macos -p agent-desktop -p agent-desktop-ffi) cargo test "${HOST_PKGS[@]}" cargo clippy "${HOST_PKGS[@]}" --all-targets -- -D warnings ``` On Windows, replace `agent-desktop-macos` in that list with `agent-desktop-windows`; on Linux, with `agent-desktop-linux`. [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) lists every gate. Build from source: [docs/install.md](docs/install.md#from-source). ## Documentation | I want to... | Read | |---|---| | Fix an install problem, grant permissions, verify a download or build from source | [docs/install.md](docs/install.md) | | Parse the JSON envelope, error codes and exit codes | [docs/json-output.md](docs/json-output.md) | | Drive the tool as an AI agent | `agent-desktop skills get desktop` ([skills/agent-desktop/](skills/agent-desktop/)) | | Learn what differs on one OS | [macOS](skills/agent-desktop-macos/), [Windows](skills/agent-desktop-windows/), [Linux](skills/agent-desktop-linux/) | | Call the C library | [skills/agent-desktop-ffi/](skills/agent-desktop-ffi/) | | Look up the vocabulary: refs, snapshots, sessions | [CONCEPTS.md](CONCEPTS.md) | | Contribute and pass the gates | [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) | | Read the engineering rules | [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) | | Learn from past bugs and lessons | [docs/solutions/](docs/solutions/) | | Find answers to common questions | [docs/faq.md](docs/faq.md) | | Report a vulnerability | [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) | | Get help | [SUPPORT.md](SUPPORT.md) | ## License Apache-2.0

# Paperclip is the app people use to manage AI agents for work. Open-source orchestration for teams of AI agents. **If OpenClaw is an _employee_, Paperclip is the _company_.** Paperclip is a Node.js server and React UI that orchestrates a team of AI agents to run a business. Bring your own agents, assign goals, and track work and costs from one dashboard. Choose models and harnesses per agent while keeping your team's tasks, skills, permissions, and history in one place. It looks like a task manager. Under the hood: org charts, budgets, governance, goal alignment, and agent coordination. **Manage business goals, not pull requests.** | | Step | Example | | ------ | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | | **01** | Define the goal | _"Build the #1 AI note-taking app to $1M MRR."_ | | **02** | Hire the team | CEO, CTO, engineers, designers, marketers — any bot, any provider. | | **03** | Approve and run | Review strategy. Set budgets. Hit go. Monitor from the dashboard. |
Works
with
OpenClaw
Claude Code
Codex
Cursor
+ Cloud
Gemini CLI

OpenCode
Pi
Hermes
+ Gateway
Grok Build
Kimi Code
If it can receive a heartbeat, it's hired.
Custom processes, HTTP endpoints, and external adapter packages extend the roster. See the [adapter overview](https://docs.paperclip.ing/reference/adapters/overview/) for setup and capabilities.
## Paperclip is right for you if - ✅ You want to build **autonomous AI organizations** - ✅ You **coordinate many different agents** (OpenClaw, Codex, Claude, Cursor) toward a common goal - ✅ You have **20 simultaneous Claude Code terminals** open and lose track of what everyone is doing - ✅ You want agents running **autonomously 24/7**, but still want to audit work and chime in when needed - ✅ You want to **monitor costs** and enforce budgets - ✅ You want a process for managing agents that **feels like using a task manager** - ✅ You want to manage your autonomous businesses **from your phone**
## The four pillars Four things have to work for an organization of AI agents to actually produce: the tasks, the org, the training, and the infrastructure. Paperclip is built around exactly those four pillars. | Pillar | Built for | What it covers | | --- | --- | --- | | **Agentic Task Manager** — Declare intent. Agents work. You verify the output. | Everyone, daily | Tasks, approvals & review gates · proactive agent coworkers · auditable routines & workflows · verify from diffs, screenshots & tests | | **Org Chart for Agents** — Roles, permissions & boundaries for humans and agents. | Managers | Mixed human + agent org chart · responsibilities, delegation, specialization · governance: who can do what · scoped secrets & company boundaries · connection permissions & responsible-user identities | | **Agent Employee Training** — Design, train & evaluate your AI employees. | Enablers | Skill Studio & shared org-wide skills · evals & saved test runs · active learning loops & quality metrics · performance reviews for agents · saved test inputs · skill version history & restore · reusable team templates | | **Agentic OS** — The infrastructure that makes the work run. | IT & platform | Cross-provider runtime: any model, any agent · sandboxing, integrations & MCP servers · SSO, GRC, RBAC & cost controls · data privacy, internal trace collection, compounding data value · personal & shared app connections · run history & opt-in tracing |
## Features

🔌 Bring Your Own Agent

Any agent, any runtime, one org chart. If it can receive a heartbeat, it's hired.

🎯 Goal Alignment

Link tasks and projects to your organization goals. Agents receive the goal context behind their work.

💓 Heartbeats

Agents wake for assigned work, follow-up messages, or configured schedules. Delegation flows up and down the org chart.

💰 Cost Control

Company, agent, and project budgets. Track reported spend, get threshold alerts, and pause work at configured limits.

🏢 Multi-Organization

One deployment, many organizations. Separate tasks, agents, permissions, and activity histories for each.

🎫 Task Threads

Keep conversations, plans, blockers, files, and run history attached to the work. Assign tasks to agents or people.

🛡️ Governance

Configure review and approval stages, approve hires, and pause, reassign, or stop work when needed.

📊 Org Chart

Hierarchies, roles, reporting lines. Your agents have a boss, a title, and a job description.

📱 Mobile Ready

Monitor and manage your autonomous businesses from anywhere.

🔗 Apps & Connections

Connect services such as GitHub, Notion, and Railway, or your own MCP server. Set gateway actions to Allowed, Ask first, or Off.

👥 Shared Agents, Personal Accounts

Choose who can use a connection and which agents can access it. Managed GitHub operations can use the account of the person directing the work.

🧠 Skills & Skill Studio

Install or write shared skills, test them with saved inputs, inspect results, and restore earlier versions.

📅 Scheduled Routines

Run recurring work on a schedule or trigger it through an API or webhook. Each run has a task, an owner, and a history.

📎 Artifacts & Feedback

Find the files and documents agents produce. Preview supported formats and leave comments on specific passages in documents.

📦 Ready-Made Teams

Preview and install teams with roles, skills, projects, and routines. Choose their runtimes and make the setup your own.
Experimental **Agent Chat** and **chat/email connectors** add conversations with agents in Paperclip and through configured services such as Slack, Discord, Telegram, and AgentMail. Enable the relevant instance settings to try them.
## Problems Paperclip solves | Without Paperclip | With Paper

VoiceStudio

AI voice studio. On your device.

Clone, design, dub, dictate, transcribe and narrate in 646 languages.

Runs on your laptop, desktop, servers, phone, tablets and more

Website · Download · Get started · Docs · Discord · 简体中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Русский

Strategic sponsors

Special sponsor


Demo workspace · Default dark theme · Watch the HD tour

## What you can do

Voice cloning
Turn a clean reference recording into speech in a familiar voice.
Video dubbing
Translate and dub videos with speech timed to the original.

Voice design
Describe a voice in words and generate it.
Local models
Choose your engines and download only the models you need.
More screenshots

Workspace overview
Model packs
- **Dictate & transcribe** — A floating dictation widget and local transcription - **Narrate & batch** — Stories, audiobooks and queued jobs - **Connect & automate** — Local API, MCP, reusable recipes and watch folders Start with **VoiceStudio** (default, powered by k2-fsa/OmniVoice), or pick from dozens of other engines in the Model Manager. See the [features & engine catalog](docs/feature-catalog.md). ## Platforms Choose your system, then expand an installation method.
macOS · Homebrew · DMG · installer
**Stable · Apple Silicon**
macOS 13.3+ · Apple Silicon: local engines with Metal (MPS). ```sh brew tap debpalash/tap brew trust --cask debpalash/tap/voicestudio brew install --cask debpalash/tap/voicestudio ```
DMG Download the DMG for your Mac, open it and drag VoiceStudio into Applications. [Download](https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio/releases/latest) · [Guide](docs/install/macos.md)
One-command installer ```sh curl -fsSL https://voicestudio.sh/install | sh ```
Intel Mac · remote backend · Limited The app UI runs on Intel; connect it to a VoiceStudio backend on another computer. [Guide](docs/install/macos.md)
> [!NOTE] > On macOS, "VoiceStudio is damaged and can't be opened" means Gatekeeper blocked the app, not that the download is broken. See the [Gatekeeper fix](docs/install/macos.md#gatekeeper-quarantine).
Windows · PowerShell · EXE
**Stable · x64**
Windows 10/11 x64 · NVIDIA CUDA · AMD ROCm (opt-in) · CPU. ```powershell irm https://voicestudio.sh/install.ps1 | iex ``` [Download the Windows installer](https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio/releases/latest) · [Guide](docs/install/windows.md) · [AMD ROCm](docs/install/windows-rocm.md)
Windows on ARM · experimental Native app UI; the x64 Python backend runs under emulation on the CPU. [Download](https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio/releases/latest) · [Guide](docs/install/windows.md)
Linux · AUR · Snap · DEB · AppImage · Nix
**Stable · x64**
Linux x64 · NVIDIA CUDA · CPU · Vulkan for supported GGUF engines.
One-command installer ```sh curl -fsSL https://voicestudio.sh/install | sh ```
Arch / Manjaro / EndeavourOS · AUR ```sh yay -S voicestudio-bin ``` Also available through `paru -S voicestudio-bin`. [Development sources](https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/voicestudio-git) · `yay -S voicestudio-git`
Build from AUR and install with pacman ```sh sudo pacman -S --needed base-devel git git clone https://aur.archlinux.org/voicestudio-bin.git cd voicestudio-bin makepkg -s sudo pacman -U ./voicestudio-bin-*.pkg.tar.zst ```
Ubuntu / Debian / Linux Mint · DEB Download the `.deb` into the current folder, then install it: [Download](https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio/releases/latest) ```sh sudo apt install ./VoiceStudio-*-linux-x64.deb ```
Snap · Ubuntu, Fedora, openSUSE and more With [snapd installed](https://snapcraft.io/docs/installing-snapd): ```sh sudo snap install voicestudio ``` To enable microphone access: ```sh sudo snap connect voicestudio:audio-record ```
Any Linux distribution · AppImage Download the AppImage into the current folder, then launch it: [Download](https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio/releases/latest) ```sh chmod +x VoiceStudio-*-linux-x64.AppImage ./VoiceStudio-*-linux-x64.AppImage ```
Nix / NixOS · source environment Enter the repository’s FHS development environment, then run from source: ```sh git clone https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio.git cd VoiceStudio nix develop .#fhs bun run dev ``` [Guide](docs/install/nix.md)
[Guide](docs/install/linux.md)
Docker · GHCR · Docker Hub
Stable images · CPU · NVIDIA CUDA · AMD ROCm.

details.readme:
Write HTML. Render video. Built for agents.

Studio | Quickstart | Showcase | Playground | Catalog | Docs | Discord

Download the desktop app: macOS · Windows · Linux (.deb)

HyperFrames is an open-source framework for turning HTML, CSS, media, and seekable animations into deterministic MP4 videos. Use it locally with the CLI, from AI coding agents with skills, or as the rendering core behind hosted authoring workflows. Using Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or another coding agent? Run `npx hyperframes skills update` once, then ask your agent to make a video. ## Quick Start ### With an AI coding agent For Claude Code, install the versioned plugin: ```bash claude plugin marketplace add heygen-com/hyperframes claude plugin install hyperframes@hyperframes ``` To enable auto-update for the **hyperframes** marketplace, run `claude` in a terminal in your project. In Claude Code's terminal UI, run `/plugin`, then select **Marketplaces** → **hyperframes** → **Enable auto-update**. Afterward, use `/hyperframes:hyperframes`. See the [plugin guide](docs/guides/plugins.mdx) for Copilot, VS Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, updates, and migration. For standalone skills (including OpenCode), use: ```bash npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes ``` > The picker opens with nothing pre-selected — the **Core Skills** group is all you need; `/slideshow`, `/remotion-to-hyperframes`, `/reverse-any-video` and `/figma` install on demand. Agents and non-interactive runs should use `npx hyperframes skills update` instead — it installs exactly the core set, whereas `skills add --all` installs all 8 published skills. The six repo-internal skills under `.claude/skills` / `.agents/skills` are excluded by default. For the full published set use `npx hyperframes skills`. > > `skills add` resolves the skills.sh registry blob, which can lag `main` by hours. `npx hyperframes skills update` installs from the current `main`, so reach for it when you need the newest copy of a skill. Run project-local installs from your video project's directory. From a HyperFrames checkout, use `npx hyperframes skills update` for a global install instead: a project-local installer target can overlap the tracked `skills/` source and overwrite uncommitted edits. See [contributor setup](CONTRIBUTING.md#getting-started). Try a prompt like: > Using `/hyperframes`, create a 10-second product intro with a fade-in title, a background video, and subtle background music. The skills teach agents the HyperFrames production loop: plan the video, write valid HTML, wire seekable animations, add media, lint, preview, and render. They work with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, IBM Bob, and other coding agents that support skills. ## Skills HyperFrames ships 8 skills. Make any video by asking for it; the `/hyperframes` skill carries the contract and the references (film, captions, overlays, motion, look). Read it first. For standalone installation, default to the **core set** (`/hyperframes`, `/hyperframes-cli`, `/hyperframes-registry`, `/media-use`). `npx hyperframes skills update` installs exactly that from anywhere; the interactive picker (`npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes`) lists it as the "Core Skills" group, nothing pre-selected. The picker is interactive-only — a non-interactive or agent run without `--skill` installs all 8. Use `npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes --all` to install the complete published set deliberately (skips the picker), or `npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes --skill ` for just one (bare name, no leading `/`). Standalone installs stay lean after that: `npx hyperframes init` installs the **core set** only when it is missing and never touches a skill you already have (`npx hyperframes skills update` refreshes them, and never removes one); `/figma`, `/slideshow`, `/remotion-to-hyperframes` and `/reverse-any-video` install **on demand** with `npx hyperframes skills update `. Nothing re-pulls the full set behind your back. ### Plugin packages Plugins bundle the full skill catalog and use their agent's update manager. `bun run package:agent-plugin` builds the committed portable ZIP, source metadata, and SHA-256 checksum. See the [maintainer checklist](docs/contributing/agent-plugins.mdx). ### Upload to Codex Build the upload-ready Codex plugin archive from the committed `HEAD` version of the manifest, brand assets, and skills: ```bash bun run package:codex-plugin ``` This writes `dist/hyperframes-plugin.zip` with a `hyperframes/` root folder and fails if the archive exceeds Codex's 100 MB upload limit. ### Core set | Skill | Use when | | ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `/hyperframes` | **Read first** for any request to make, edit, animate or render a video, motion graphic, captions or overlays with HyperFrames (HTML rendered to video). Holds the render contract and the work loop, and points to the references for format, motion, look, captions, whole films and storyboards. | | `/hyperframes-cli` | The HyperFrames CLI by job — scaffold, check, look at frames, edit the timeline, preview, render locally or in the cloud, publish, project history — plus reading its JSON and recovering from build or render failures. | | `/hyperframes-registry` | About 450 ready-made blocks and components installed as editable source — transitions, overlays, titles, kinetic type, captions, charts, maps, 3D, camera moves. Use before hand-building any named visual; also for `hyperframes add` and `catalog`. | | `/media-use` | Get or make any media for a video — music, sound effects, images, icons, logos, voiceover, avatar and generated video, transcripts, cutouts, colour grades and looks — with HeyGen or free local tools, and mix placed audio. Also for footage that looks dark, flat or dull. | ### On demand | Skill | Use when | | -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `/figma` | Bring Figma into a video — rendered assets, brand tokens, components, storyboard frames as reconstructed motion, shaders and connector-assisted motion. Use when you paste a figma.com link. | | `/slideshow` | A presentation, pitch deck or interactive deck — discrete slides, fragment reveals, branching, hotspot navigation, presenter mode with speaker notes. Output is a navigable deck, not a rendered MP4. | | `/remotion-to-hyperframes` | Bringing existing video code or footage into HyperFrames (Remotion first; also Motion Canvas, Lottie, Three.js, canvas, other tools' renders), verified frame by frame. | | `/reverse-any-video` | Rebuilding any video file as an editable HyperFrames project (motion graphics, talking heads, live action, AI-generated footage), checked frame by frame against the original. HyperFrames Pro. | For visual design handoff workflows, see the [Claude Design guide](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/guides/claude-design) and [Open Design guide](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/guides/open-design). ### Manually with the CLI ```bash npx hyperframes init my-video cd my-video npx hyperframes preview # preview in browser with live reload npx hyperframes render # render to MP4 ``` **Requirements:** Node.js 22+, FFmpeg ## What You Can Build Need ideas? Browse the [Showcase](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/showcase) for finished videos you can watch, read, run, and remix. - Product launch videos and feature announcements - PR walkthroughs with animated code diffs, narration, and captions - Data visualizations, chart races, and map animations - Social videos with kinetic captions, overlays, and music - Docs-to-video, PDF-to-video, and site-tour explainers - Reusable motion graphics for automated content pipelines ## Frame.md **frame.md — your design system, ready for video.** Every brand has a `design.md`. None of them were written for a camera. `frame.md` is the missing translation layer: it takes your web-context design spec and inverts it for the frame — the same tokens, the same rules, but rewritten so an AI agent can compose a promo video without guessing at scale or reaching for web chrome. The output is a `DESIGN.md` superset your whole toolchain can read. Atoms stay sacred. Composition stays free. Numbers come from the script.

Biennale Yellow

details.readme:
# Speech Studio **Free, offline AI voice studio for Windows, macOS (Apple silicon) and Linux — voice any text with cloned and built-in voices, and turn recordings into text with the speakers. Russian done right: numbers in their cases, stress marks, «ё» and homographs. 100% local, zero Python: one native app (Rust + C++ on CUDA, Vulkan or Metal); every model and engine downloads with a button.** [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/timoncool/speech-studio?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) [![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/timoncool/speech-studio?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/timoncool/speech-studio/stargazers) [![Latest release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/timoncool/speech-studio?include_prereleases&style=flat-square)](https://github.com/timoncool/speech-studio/releases) [![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/timoncool/speech-studio/total?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/timoncool/speech-studio/releases) [![Last commit](https://img.shields.io/github/last-commit/timoncool/speech-studio?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/timoncool/speech-studio/commits) **English** · [Русский](README.ru.md) · [中文](README.zh.md) · [Español](README.es.md) · [Português](README.pt.md) · [Français](README.fr.md) ![Speech Studio — a voiced dialog with a voice per character](docs/screenshots/en-01-speech.webp)
## What it is **Speech Studio** has three modes. **Speech** voices text: a line, a dialog with a voice per character, a podcast the director writes for you, or a whole book from EPUB, FB2, PDF or DOCX. **Listening** turns a recording, a video or a link into text with who said what and when, cuts it by its words, checks a voicing against the text it should say and makes library voices from its speakers. **Live** is a voice conversation with an AI agent connected over MCP: it says each phrase as soon as it writes it and hears you through the microphone. Everything runs **locally on your machine** — no cloud, no subscription; your texts, recordings and voiceprints never leave your computer. If you want a voice your card can't run, the cloud voices of **OpenRouter**, **Google Gemini**, **fal.ai** and **Runware** are there too, each behind its own key and a confirmation before the first call; they are off by default. It's a **fully native app**: no embeddable Python, no torch, no CUDA wheels. The whole studio is **Rust + native C++ engines (GGUF/ONNX) on CUDA, Vulkan or Metal**. Models, engines, the CUDA and VC++ runtimes and ffmpeg are **downloaded by the app itself** on first run, and a model another of the author's studios already has is taken from it instead of downloaded again. **An NVIDIA GPU is what the app is built and tested for**; see *What runs where* for the rest. ## For AI agents While Speech Studio is open it serves MCP at `http://127.0.0.1:8797/mcp`: an agent such as Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor or Codex does everything the window does, through the same code — voices a text into a file in one call, makes and edits projects block by block, casts voices to characters, designs a voice from a description, transcribes and checks recordings, exports audiobooks with chapters and subtitles. Settings, **Agent (MCP)** shows whether an agent is connected and what to paste into the client. The one thing an agent cannot do is turn the microphone on: Live, a recording and the microphone test start only on your own click or key. 1. Install the studio from the [latest release](https://github.com/timoncool/speech-studio/releases/latest) and start it. 2. Connect to its MCP server: ```bash claude mcp add --transport http speech-studio http://127.0.0.1:8797/mcp ``` Other clients: `{ "mcpServers": { "speech-studio": { "type": "streamable-http", "url": "http://127.0.0.1:8797/mcp" } } }` 3. Read the skill the server serves (resource `studio://skill`), the same text as [docs/mcp-skill.md](docs/mcp-skill.md), and start with the tool `studio_status`. The studio also speaks the OpenAI audio API on the same port — `POST /v1/audio/speech`, `POST /v1/audio/transcriptions`, `GET /v1/models` — so tools written for OpenAI voice and transcribe through it, with a library voice's name as `voice`. [llms.txt](llms.txt) says the same for tools that look for it. Only programs on this computer may connect. ## What you can make with it - **An audiobook** — drop an EPUB or FB2: chapters, characters with their own voices, an M4B with chapters and cover, ACX loudness checked. - **A podcast or a dialog** — the director writes a podcast on a topic for two or three speakers, or paste lines like «Anna: …»; the timeline shows every overlap. - **A voice-over for a video** — voice a script or subtitles into their cues, lay music and sounds under it in the track editor, export at the video's loudness. - **A transcript of an interview or a lecture** — who said what and when, word times, subtitles by broadcasters' rules, the recording cut by its text. - **A check of a dubbing** — lay the script over the recording and see every word said wrong or skipped. - **Your own voice library** — record or import voices, clean them, make voices from the speakers of a recording. - **A voice for your AI agent** — talk with Claude Code or any MCP agent in Live, or let it voice and transcribe files through MCP or the OpenAI-compatible API. Examples of every engine and voice, with Russian stress before and after, are on the [project page](https://timoncool.github.io/speech-studio/). ## Three modes | Mode | What it does | |------|--------------| | 🔊 **Speech** | Text, dialog, podcast or book → voiced blocks with takes, checked by ear, exported as WAV, FLAC, MP3, OGG, M4A or M4B with chapters, subtitles and synced text | | 👂 **Listening** | Audio, video or a link → a transcript with speakers and word times, a karaoke player, cut-by-text, export to SRT, VTT, ASS, TXT or JSON, a check against a reference text | | 🎙️ **Live** | A voice conversation with an AI agent: the agent connected over MCP speaks each phrase as it writes it, you answer into the microphone and are recognised phrase by phrase, a phrase said over it stops it; only you turn the microphone on, pause with M or Ctrl+Shift+Space, a widget over every window | ## Features **Voices and engines** - **Five local engines** — [Higgs Audio v3](https://huggingface.co/bosonai) (cloning, emotions and sounds), **Fish Audio Drama 3** (the strongest open voice; the whole model on a 24 GB card, from 6 GB with its experts in RAM), **Supertonic 3** (fast, ten built-in voices), **Qwen3-TTS 1.7B** (nine built-in voices, cloning, an instruction per block) and **Qwen3-TTS with Russian stress**, siriusfreak's LoRA applied at run time. - **Engine per character and per block** over the project's own; an engine that can't speak the voice in use says which of its voices it takes. - **Voice library** — a voice pack in one click, 743 Russian voices from the cloud catalogue, recording from the microphone, import of files and ZIPs, photo, gender, age, language, tags and consent; the reference transcript is recognised once and kept. - **Clean a reference** — Mel-Band Roformer takes the voice from music, **DPDFNet** takes noise away with a strength control so speech stays alive; the original is kept. - **Best piece of a reference** — windows at pauses between recognised words, each with its length, signal-to-noise, clipping and longest pause. - **Voice by description** — Qwen3-TTS VoiceDesign makes a voice from "an elderly woman with a soft, slightly hoarse voice…": hear several candidates, keep one in the library. - **Cloud voices** — OpenRouter, Google Gemini (parallel requests or Batch at half the price), fal.ai and Runware, each behind its own key and a confirmation before the first call. **Text that sounds right** - **Russian normaliser** — numbers in the right case and gender, dates, times, money, units, Roman numerals, Latin brand names and abbreviations. - **Stress, «ё» and homographs** by RUAccent — the large homograph model (big_poetry in int8, the same choices as fp32) picks замо́к or за́мок by the sentence; doubtful ones are highlighted for you, your own `+` marks stay. - **Pronunciation dictionary** — replace, regex and phonemes, scoped to the project, a language, a voice or an engine, Balabolka `.rex`/`.dic`/`.bxd` import, and a check by ear right from the dictionary. - **SpeechKit-compatible markup** — `+` stress, `sil<[300]>` and `[pause 500ms]` pauses, `[rate:1.2]` tempo, `**accent**`; what an engine ignores is marked, never silently dropped. - **More of the text read right** — an SSML subset, prosody hints coloured word by word, phone numbers, e-mail addresses and codes, a passage in another language in the same voice, and a check of the script before voicing. **Projects** - **Text as the timeline** — blocks with speakers, takes (up to five), stale tracking, undo and redo, drag to reorder, search and replace with regex, notes and markers. - **Quality control** — every take recognised back and compared word by word, plus checks for clipping, silence, cut-off, a click at the end, a repeated phrase, a long tail, music or noise instead of speech, and similarity to the reference voice; several takes with the best one picked. - **Dialog and podcasts** — `Anna:` and `[Anna]` lines become characters, the director writes a podcast on a topic for N speakers, negative pauses make interruptions, and the **timeline** shows every overlap with cut, join or keep. - **Audiobooks** — EPUB, FB2, PDF, DOCX, HTML, Markdown and TXT with chapter preview, cast by the director, M4B with chapters and cover, parts for long books, ACX loudness check. - **Subtitles as a project** — SRT, VTT and ASS lines voiced into their cues: the tempo raised ahead, a retry when a take doesn't fit, then stretching and borrowing the silence before the line. - **Export check** — blocks missing, stale, failed, with a changed file or too long for their cue are listed before export; only the length may be allowed through. - **Loudness** — video (−14 LUFS), podcast (−16 LUFS) and ACX presets with a true-peak limiter, room tone and breaths between blocks. - **Project file** — `.speechproj` with text, voices and audio carries a project to another computer. - **Montage** — a track editor under the text: move, trim, fade and level each clip, music and sound tracks from files or folders, or a song made right there in YuE2, MiniMax Music3 or ACE-Step Studio. - **Export for every use** — a file per chapter, a track per character in a ZIP, a CSV table of lines, voice effects (radio, phone, loudspeaker), even loudness of pieces, sample rate and bit depth, file name templates, a SHA-256 manifest and a note on how it was made. - **Compare and approve** — A/B of takes, a blind comparison of engines on the same text, approved blocks a re-voicing leaves alone, a quality traffic light and a project report. - **Books and plays** — direct speech apart from the author's, a cast of characters with voices picked for them, footnotes cleaned out, the book's names into the dictionary, a project updated from a corrected book without losing what is voiced, and an HTML player of the book. **Listening** - **Parakeet-TDT v3, Nemotron 3.5 (28 languages with punctuation) and CrisperWhisper 2.0 turbo (99 languages with word times) on audio.cpp, Parakeet Ultra on transcribe.cpp**, up to eight speakers by Nemotron 3 Diarization, a long recording cut at pauses by **Silero VAD v6**, noise removed by DPDFNet, music removed by Roformer. - **A hint for CrisperWhisper** — topic and spellings, plus the corrections you add. - **Batch** — drop several files at once; each becomes a recording queued for recognition. - **Lay a known text over the recording** — the reference text takes the time of each heard word, sentence by sentence. - **Voices from speakers** — a library voice f

details.readme:
Concat

The free, open-source, cross-platform CapCut replacement.

**🇬🇧 English** · [🇩🇪 Deutsch](docs/README.de.md) · [🇪🇸 Español](docs/README.es.md) · [🇫🇷 Français](docs/README.fr.md) · [🇮🇹 Italiano](docs/README.it.md) · [🇳🇱 Nederlands](docs/README.nl.md) · [🇵🇱 Polski](docs/README.pl.md) · [🇧🇷 Português (Brasil)](docs/README.pt-BR.md) · [🇷🇺 Русский](docs/README.ru.md) · [🇺🇦 Українська](docs/README.uk.md) · [🇹🇷 Türkçe](docs/README.tr.md) · [🇦🇿 Azərbaycanca](docs/README.az.md) · [🇭🇷 Hrvatski](docs/README.hr.md) · [🇮🇩 Bahasa Indonesia](docs/README.id.md) · [🇻🇳 Tiếng Việt](docs/README.vi.md) · [🇹🇭 ไทย](docs/README.th.md) · [🇯🇵 日本語](docs/README.ja.md) · [🇰🇷 한국어](docs/README.ko.md) · [🇨🇳 简体中文](docs/README.zh-Hans.md) · [🇹🇼 繁體中文](docs/README.zh-TW.md) · [🇸🇦 العربية](docs/README.ar.md) · [🇮🇱 עברית](docs/README.he.md) · [🇮🇷 فارسی](docs/README.fa.md) · [🇮🇳 हिन्दी](docs/README.hi.md) · [🇵🇰 اردو](docs/README.ur.md) · [🇧🇩 বাংলা](docs/README.bn.md) ## Paid Sponsors

we have come too far to back down now 😢
## About Concat is a free, open-source video editor and a CapCut alternative for macOS, Windows, Linux and Android. It covers what people actually open CapCut for: auto-captions, text-to-speech, background removal, keyframe animation, effects and titles, multi-track cutting, 4K export. With none of the catches: no watermark, no account, no subscription, no upload. Everything runs locally on a native Rust engine with a GPU compositor. Install it, drop in footage, cut. The AI models for captions, voices and cutout download once from Settings and work offline after that. Your footage never leaves your disk. **Good for:** TikTok, Reels and Shorts, YouTube videos, tutorials and screen recordings, podcast clips, memes. **Also for machines:** a built-in MCP server for AI agents (`concat --mcp`, [set up](docs/MCP.md)) and a JSON-RPC API for scripts, so they can cut video with it too. ## Highlights - 🚫 **No watermarks. No account. No paywall.** Ever. - 🔒 **100% local.** Nothing uploads. Works offline. - 💬 **Auto-captions.** Local Whisper. Pick a model size, get styled captions on the timeline. - 🗣️ **Text-to-speech + voice cloning.** Free local voices, or any voice from a few seconds of a recording. - 🧍 **Background removal.** People, objects, or paint the mask yourself. - 🎞️ **Keyframes.** Position, scale, rotation, opacity, volume, effect parameters. Curve editor built in. - ✨ **100 effects, filters and transitions.** GPU-rendered, live in the preview. - ✂️ **Cut fast.** Split, trim, ripple, merge, freeze frame, speed. Magnetic timeline if you want it. - 🎚️ **Multi-track, multi-timeline.** Overlays and picture-in-picture: stack video, stills and titles on as many tracks as you like. Several cuts in one project. Blend modes (screen, add, multiply…), crop, flips. - 📝 **Titles.** Fonts, stroke, shadow, background plate. Presets to start from. - 🎙️ **One-switch voice cleanup.** Denoise, enhance voice, level the loudness. Plus chipmunk, robot, telephone and friends. - 📤 **Export.** H.264, HEVC, AV1. Up to 4K 60, 10-bit colour. - 🦀 **Native Rust engine.** GPU compositor, proxies, hardware decode. 4K scrubs smoothly. - 🤖 **Scriptable.** An MCP server built in, so Claude and other AI agents can edit with it ([one line to set up](docs/MCP.md)), and a JSON-RPC API for scripts. A build from source adds gRPC and a command-line tool. - 🖥️ **macOS, Windows, Linux, Android.** 26 languages. Same app, same project files. ## Download Two ways in: 1. **[The website](https://concat.standalones.org/#download)** hands you the right build for your machine. Start here. 2. **[GitHub Releases](https://github.com/jub0t/Concat/releases)** has every build for every platform, with installers, packages and checksums. For when you want to pick. Concat is in **beta**: it works, and it still has edges. [Say so](https://github.com/jub0t/Concat/issues) when you find one. **Platforms** - ✅ **Windows** · x86_64 (ARM builds are paused, see [#326](https://github.com/jub0t/Concat/issues/326)). A setup and an `.msi`. If SmartScreen stops an unsigned build: **More info** › **Run anyway** - ✅ **macOS** · Intel and Apple silicon. If macOS refuses to open an unsigned build: `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Concat.app` - ✅ **Linux** · x86_64 and ARM. `.deb`, `.rpm`, `.AppImage` and an Arch package. Also a Flatpak on **[Flatpark](https://flatpark.org/apps/app.concat.editor/)**, a community Flatpak remote that wraps the x86_64 `.deb` of each release and updates with it - ✅ **Android** · phones and tablets - ✅ **iOS / iPadOS** · iPhone and iPad, sideloaded ✅ Supported · 🚧 Work in progress · 🧪 To be tested **System requirements** and the optional model sizes are on [the website](https://concat.standalones.org/guides/system-requirements). **[Code signing policy](CODE_SIGNING.md)**: why the Windows builds are not signed yet, and what Concat sends over the network (nothing you did not ask for). ## Build from source You need Rust 1.93 or newer (see `rust-version` in `src/Cargo.toml`), the FFmpeg 7+ development libraries, cmake and a C++ compiler. - **macOS:** `brew install ffmpeg` - **Windows:** from [FFmpeg's Windows downloads](https://ffmpeg.org/download.html#build-windows), take BtbN's `win64-gpl-shared` build (the one CI uses), unpack it and point `FFMPEG_DIR` at it - **Linux:** use your distro's FFmpeg if it is version 7 or newer, otherwise use a BtbN `shared` build with `FFMPEG_DIR` like on Windows Then: ```sh cd src cargo run -p concat # the editor window ``` Other useful commands: ```sh cargo build --profile app -p concat # the shipping binary (fat LTO, stripped) cargo test # run the test suite cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings # what CI checks ``` If you change text the interface shows, run `python3 scripts/locales.py` from the repo root so the string inventory stays in sync. Full details live in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## How to Contribute > [!IMPORTANT] > The best way to contribute is to grab a build from the [Releases](https://github.com/jub0t/Concat/releases) page and use it: find where it breaks, and say where it could be better. > > Ready to write code? [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) covers setup, the layout of the tree, the checks to run, and how contributions are licensed. Driving Concat from a script, a service or an agent? [The developer docs](https://concat.standalones.org/docs) cover the Concat API and its transports: JSON-RPC and gRPC; [docs/MCP.md](docs/MCP.md) connects an AI agent over MCP. [This Discussion](https://github.com/jub0t/Concat/discussions/3) is where the project was announced. > > Contributors can claim a `@Contributor` role in the Discord server: just ask. ## Star History ## Contributors ## Licence Concat is free software under [AGPL-3.0-or-later](LICENSE).
